title: Shrapnel
tagline: An uncontained engine failure climbing out of Brize Norton.
history: Inspired by a 2010 uncontained engine failure on a four-engine airliner, whose debris cut fuel, hydraulic and electrical lines; the crew worked through dozens of checklists and landed heavy on a long runway, with partial brakes, without injury.
situation: Heavy C-5 out of RAF Brize Norton's runway 25, climbing through 3,500 ft with 73 aboard, when number 2 lets go. Debris has gone through the left wing. You are heavy, leaking fuel, and short of hydraulics and brakes — but the aircraft flies.
tips: Fly the aircraft first: rudder against the dead engine, keep the speed
Long final to runway 07 or 25 (3,050 m) — every metre counts with weak brakes
Gear may need the alternate extension (O → Systems)
Full reverse on the good engines, brakes early and firm

do.note: Engineer: Number two's gone — uncontained! Fuel leak left wing, hydraulic two's down, generator two offline.
ATC: Both runway ends available, fire service positioning at the mid-point.

objectives.text: Land and stop on the runway
